entries: Nobody invented electricity: it is a natural force. Benjamin Franklin showed lightning is electricity (1752), Alessandro Volta made the first battery (1800), Michael Faraday invented the electric generator (1831), and Thomas Edison and Nikola Tesla built power systems.
Martin Cooper of Motorola made the first handheld mobile phone call in 1973. The first iPhone (Apple, Steve Jobs) came in 2007 and made touchscreen smartphones popular.

The internet grew from ARPANET (1969, USA). Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn created TCP/IP (1974), the rules the internet still uses, so they are called the fathers of the internet. Tim Berners-Lee later invented the World Wide Web (1989).
Karl Benz built the first practical petrol car, the Benz Patent-Motorwagen, in 1885–86. Henry Ford made cars cheap with the Model T and the moving assembly line (1908–1913).
Karl von Drais made the first two-wheeled 'running machine' (no pedals) in 1817. Pedals were added in the 1860s, and John Kemp Starley's 'safety bicycle' (1885) looks like today's bicycles.

George Stephenson built the Locomotion No. 1 (1825) and the Rocket (1829), the first successful steam railway engines; he is called the father of railways. India's first passenger train ran from Bombay to Thane on 16 April 1853.

Joseph Nicéphore Niépce took the first surviving photograph in 1826. Louis Daguerre made photography practical in 1839, and George Eastman's Kodak (1888) made cameras popular. The first digital camera was made by Steven Sasson at Kodak in 1975.
Jacob Perkins built the first working vapour-compression refrigerator in 1834. Electric home fridges became common in the 1920s–30s.

Zacharias Janssen is credited with the first compound microscope (around 1590). Antonie van Leeuwenhoek greatly improved single-lens microscopes and first saw bacteria (1670s); Robert Hooke named 'cells' (1665).
Alessandro Volta invented the first battery, the voltaic pile, in 1800. The unit volt is named after him.
Michael Faraday showed the first electric motor in 1821 and discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831, which led to generators and transformers.
Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics (1901).
Galileo made an early thermoscope (1593). Daniel Fahrenheit made the mercury thermometer (1714), and Anders Celsius proposed the Celsius scale (1742).
Christopher Latham Sholes invented the first practical typewriter in 1868, including the QWERTY keyboard layout we still use.
Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse in the 1960s; it was a wooden box with two wheels.
Larry Page and Sergey Brin created Google in 1998 as Stanford PhD students. Sundar Pichai, from Chennai, became Google's CEO in 2015.
Mark Zuckerberg created Facebook in 2004 with college friends at Harvard University. The company is now called Meta and also owns Instagram and WhatsApp.
YouTube was created in 2005 by Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim. The first video was 'Me at the zoo'. Google bought it in 2006.
WhatsApp was created in 2009 by Jan Koum and Brian Acton. Facebook (Meta) bought it in 2014.
Python was created by Guido van Rossum, first released in 1991. It is named after the comedy show Monty Python, not the snake.
Java was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems and released in 1995. It was first called Oak.
The C language was created by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs in 1972. C++ was created by Bjarne Stroustrup in 1985.
JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich at Netscape in just 10 days in 1995.
Linus Torvalds created the Linux kernel in 1991 as a student in Finland. He also created Git in 2005.
Reed pens and quills were used for thousands of years. Lewis Waterman made a reliable fountain pen (1884), and László Bíró invented the ballpoint pen (1938).
Cai Lun of China is credited with inventing paper around 105 CE, from tree bark, hemp and rags.
The wheel was invented about 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia (modern Iraq), first for pottery and then for carts. Nobody knows the inventor's name.
Early people used sundials and water clocks. Mechanical clocks appeared in Europe in the 1300s, and Christiaan Huygens invented the accurate pendulum clock in 1656.
Willis Carrier invented the modern air conditioner in 1902 to control humidity in a printing factory.
Alva Fisher is often credited with the first electric washing machine, the Thor (1908).
Percy Spencer invented the microwave oven in 1945 after a chocolate bar melted in his pocket near a radar machine.
Igor Sikorsky built the first practical helicopter, the VS-300, in 1939.
Cornelis Drebbel built the first navigable submarine in 1620. John Holland built the first modern submarine for the US Navy in 1900.
The Chinese used gunpowder rockets over 800 years ago. Tipu Sultan used iron-cased Mysorean rockets against the British in the 1780s–90s. Robert Goddard launched the first liquid-fuel rocket in 1926.
Eugene Polley invented the first wireless TV remote, the Flash-Matic, in 1955.
Masahiro Hara of Denso Wave (Japan) invented the QR code in 1994 to track car parts.
Louis Braille, who was blind from age three, invented the Braille reading system of raised dots in 1824, when he was just 15.
Gitanjali was written by Rabindranath Tagore. Its English version won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, the first for an Asian.
Jana Gana Mana, India's national anthem, was written by Rabindranath Tagore. Vande Mataram, the national song, was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
Abhijnanashakuntalam (The Recognition of Shakuntala) was written by Kalidasa, the great Sanskrit poet, who also wrote Meghaduta and Raghuvamsha.
Godan was written by Munshi Premchand, the great Hindi and Urdu novelist, who also wrote Nirmala, Gaban and Idgah.
Who wrote The God of Small Things?
The God of Small Things was written by Arundhati Roy; it won the Booker Prize in 1997.
who wrote the god of small things
Midnight's Children was written by Salman Rushdie; it won the Booker Prize in 1981.
The White Tiger was written by Aravind Adiga; it won the Booker Prize in 2008.
Ignited Minds was written by Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, who also wrote Wings of Fire and India 2020.
Oliver Twist was written by Charles Dickens (1838), who also wrote A Christmas Carol, Great Expectations and David Copperfield.
Who wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer?
The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (1876) and Huckleberry Finn were written by Mark Twain.
Robinson Crusoe (1719) was written by Daniel Defoe.
Gulliver's Travels (1726) was written by Jonathan Swift.
Treasure Island (1883) was written by Robert Louis Stevenson.
Who wrote The Lord of the Rings?
The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit were written by J. R. R. Tolkien.
who wrote lord of the rings
Who wrote The Chronicles of Narnia?
The Chronicles of Narnia were written by C. S. Lewis, starting with The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (1950).
who wrote the chronicles of narnia
Who wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory?
Charlie and the Chocolate Factory was written by Roald Dahl, who also wrote Matilda, The BFG and James and the Giant Peach.
who wrote charlie and the chocolate factory
Who wrote The Diary of a Young Girl?
The Diary of a Young Girl was written by Anne Frank, a Jewish girl who hid from the Nazis in Amsterdam during World War II.
who wrote diary of a young girl
The Little Prince (1943) was written by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, a French pilot.
The Sherlock Holmes stories were written by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, starting with A Study in Scarlet (1887).
The Alchemist (1988) was written by Paulo Coelho of Brazil.
On the Origin of Species (1859) was written by Charles Darwin and explained evolution by natural selection.
Who wrote A Brief History of Time?
A Brief History of Time (1988) was written by Stephen Hawking.
who wrote a brief history of time
Das Kapital was written by Karl Marx; with Friedrich Engels he also wrote The Communist Manifesto (1848).
Parthiban Kanavu, Sivagamiyin Sabatham and Ponniyin Selvan were written by Kalki Krishnamurthy.
G. U. Pope, a Christian missionary, translated the Thirukkural into English in 1886 as The Sacred Kural.
